doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Creed Taylor and the Half Note comeback
summary: Creed Taylor books them at the Half Note with Ron Carter, Jack DeJohnette and Dave Friedman, restoring the joy of music.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And our dear friend, Creed Taylor, who we’d recorded for many times, said, “listen, it’s about time you guys start to do something.” I said, “gee I don’t know, Creed.” Well he says, “I’ve got an opening for you at the Half Note.”

The Half Note in New York City on 56th street, it used to be there. And he said, “I’m going to get you a group and you’re going to go into the Half Note and you’re going to start performing again.” Okay. So it was a date like a month away, and he got us Ron Carter on bass, Jack DeJohnette on drums, and Dave Friedman on vibes. And okay I’m writing parts and doing my parts, and not coming out with it, and put this together. We had sort of a piecemeal rehearsal. First we’d rehearse with Ron Carter, then Jack
DeJohnette would be able to come in, then Dave Friedman would come in, and finally opening night and we go in and these guys were such whizzes —
— that it was just uplifting. This wonderful music we were making together. So all of a sudden the joy of making music, making good music with a group is a great experience.
